news.text: 7 June saw Dublin teen pop quartet **B*Witched** leap straight to number one on the UK singles chart with their infectious debut *C'est la Vie*. Sporting matching head-to-toe double denim and executing lightning-fast traditional Irish step-dancing, the four singers unleashed a relentless pop hurricane of tin whistles and cheerful innuendo. The track instantly took up permanent residence inside the heads of British school pupils, making denim waistcoats an inescapable summer uniform.

news.text: 12 June saw Namco release the home conversion of fighting tour-de-force *Tekken 3* for the **PlayStation** across Europe, pushing Sony's 32-bit hardware to its absolute limit. Introducing capoeira fighter Eddy Gordo, kickboxer Bryan Fury, and martial artist Ling Xiaoyu, the game delivered blistering 60-frames-per-second animation alongside the bizarre volleyball-inspired mini-game *Tekken Ball*. Players rapidly discovered that button-mashing Eddy Gordo's handstand kicks was practically guaranteed to ruin lifelong school friendships.

25 June saw Microsoft officially release **Windows 98** to retail stores worldwide, cementing Bill Gates' hegemony over home personal computing. The operating system integrated Internet Explorer directly into the desktop interface and offered plug-and-play support for new-fangled USB peripherals, banishing the nightmarish hardware conflicts of the dial-up era. Millions of computer owners eagerly handed over their cash, politely ignoring the fact that Bill Gates had suffered an embarrassing blue-screen crash while demonstrating it live two months earlier.

28 June saw professional wrestling history etched in blood and steel at *King of the Ring* in Pittsburgh during the legendary **Hell in a Cell** match. In a moment that stunned the arena, **The Undertaker** hurled Mankind (Mick Foley) from the roof of the 16-foot steel cage, sending him crashing through the Spanish announce table and prompting Jim Ross's agonised cry: "Good God Almighty! They've killed him!" Foley astonishingly climbed back up, only to be chokeslammed through the cage roof and knocked unconscious, cementing his reputation as the sport's immortal stuntman.

news.text: 29 June saw British studio Rare and Nintendo launch 3D platformer *Banjo-Kazooie* on the **Nintendo 64** in North America, raising the bar for colourful collect-a-thons. Pairing a mild-mannered honey bear with a gloriously ill-mannered red-crested breegull stuffed inside his backpack, the game dazzled players with seamlessly transforming hub worlds and witty musical jibberish dialogue. Gruntilda the witch gave evil rhyming insults, while players spent countless summer hours scouring every square inch of Mumbo's Mountain for stray golden Jiggies.

news.text: 30 June saw England suffer a heart-wrenching World Cup exit against fierce rivals Argentina in a dramatic last-16 encounter in Saint-Étienne. After 18-year-old **Michael Owen** scored an electrifying solo wondergoal, midfielder **David Beckham** was red-carded early in the second half for petulantly flicking his boot at Diego Simeone. England battled heroically with ten men before inevitably losing on penalties, leaving British tabloids to hang effigies of Beckham outside London pubs and mourn their traditional tournament fate.
